question_text: This game is recommended as an educational pastime for children, with its appeal coming not just from the competition but also a knowledge-based experience that taps into human curiosity. This game has also been part of the TechOlympics. United Kingdom and USA are "banned" from some of the serious competitions. Annie Rauwerda, who placed third in the game in 2023, notes: "I think it's exciting because you realize that almost everything in the world is connected." What are we talking about / ID the game.

The Russian company WBD (now owned by Pepsi) was founded in 1992 and given an English sounding name to seem more appealing, sophisticated and perhaps English to the post-Soviet world. The question slide shows the WBD company logo, including its Cyrillic branding. What does WBD stand for?

In September 2023, Netflix released a 5 minute sketch to a particular demographic to promote their popular TV series, Sex Education. The sketch was called X's Driving School as an ode to one of X's successful movies, Driving School. X made her debut as an 18 year old and has a filmography of over 250 films. A titular biopic on X was also directed in 2020. ID X.
answer_text: Shakeela, the Indian actress; Netflix's Sex Education promo sketch was titled "Shakeela's Driving School"

question_text: Part of the Swiss "Compagnie Financiere Richemont SA" holding company, which owns some iconic brands like IWC Schaffhausen, Piaget, and Van Cleef & Arpels, this brand was founded by Alfred Nehemias, a Hamburg banker, and August Eberstein, a Berlin engineer. The first flagship model was called "Rouge et Noir," which at the time was considered a technical achievement as it overcame the requirement of a repeated frequent action for its utilization. About 20 years later, they came out with a "masterpiece," the premium flagship product that still sells today. ID the brand.

Mimetic architecture is when the design of a structure is meant to mimic the function or purpose the building serves. It began as a form of direct marketing with instant recall. This four storey building opened in 2012 and houses the national HQ of the mimetic inspiration. Clad in stainless steel panels, it is completely raised off the ground on pale blue columns to create an impression of open space underneath (apart from the central core). At night, blue purple spotlights illuminate the building to give an illusion of it 'floating'. It is considered one of the boldest, crudest examples of mimetic architecture in modern times. If you are wondering how to get here, you can just put X building on Google Maps. What building / location?
answer_text: Fish Building, Hyderabad, home of the National Fisheries Development Board

question_text: X is a Norwegian manufacturer of certain items of which John Lasseter was a huge fan. John incorporated one such item in one of his iconic creations, named after X. This creative depiction has become associated with the identity of company Y and is in fact the first such work by Y. In 2009, when Y started offering merchandise and operating an animatronic version at the Disney theme park, X sued Y for IP infringement, resulting in a settlement where Y refrained from selling the items, the theme park installation was removed, and X would permit the use/incorporation of its product in Y's works. ID X and Y.
answer_text: X = Luxo Inc., the Norwegian lamp manufacturer; Y = Pixar, referencing the short film Luxo Jr.

question_text: Connect / give the funda for the following (illustrative 7 of an exhaustive list): Bushu Tama Gawa; Aoyama Enza-no-matsu; Toto Asakusa Hongan-ji; Soshu Umezawa-no-hidari; Koshu Kajikazawa; Shinshu Suwa-ko; Totomi San-chu.
answer_text: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the woodblock print series by Hokusai; each title names a province/location paired with a view of Mount Fuji

question_text: Dozens of sunk warships, believed to contain the remains of thousands of British, American, Australian, Dutch and Japanese servicemen from the Second World War, have been illegally ripped apart by salvage divers for years. In May 2023, a Chinese vessel was caught plundering HMS Prince of Wales and HMS Repulse, both sunk by Japanese forces in the 1940s. While sunken treasures are explored routinely, what about these ships attracted the salvage divers? Give the funda.
answer_text: Radiation-free, low-background steel, since these pre-1945 shipwrecks contain steel uncontaminated by the radionuclides released by later nuclear weapons testing

question_text: Most democracies permit any elected member of the house to propose a law, though very few succeed in pushing the law through. In 2017, Representative Mike Quigley introduced the Communications Over Various Feeds Electronically for Engagement Act (H.R. 2884) to require the National Archives to preserve a blank item. The Bill was forwarded to the House Oversight and Reform Committee and never saw the light of day. Give the funda for the blank.
answer_text: Social media interactions/posts of the President, illustrated with Donald Trump's "covfefe" tweet

question_text: In May 2020, during a possible locust swarm attack in Delhi, short of invoking the provisions of the East Punjab Agricultural Pests, Diseases and Noxious Weeds Act, 1949, summoning all able-bodied people to volunteer in defense, the government of Delhi issued a public advisory largely focusing on: (i) organising awareness; and (ii) spraying of prescribed pesticides in an innovative manner to use a characteristic of locusts against the locusts. What was this innovative idea?
answer_text: Do not let the locusts rest at night: since locust swarms fly by day and rest at night, the advisory called for disturbing them and not allowing them to rest at night so they could be targeted more effectively

question_text: This is a scene from South Park: "X: I have one final thing I want you to consider. Ladies and gentlemen, this is Chewbacca. Chewbacca is a Wookiee from the planet Kashyyyk. But Chewbacca lives on the planet Endor. Now think about it; that does not make sense! Why would a Wookiee, an 8-foot-tall Wookiee, want to live on Endor, with a bunch of 2-foot-tall Ewoks? That does not make sense! But more important, you have to ask yourself: What does this have to do with this case? Nothing." This gave rise to a now popularly recognised defense strategy called the Chewbacca defense, used when a jury is overwhelmed with irrelevant non sequiturs which lead them to ignore or overlook other glaring evidence. What/who was the inspiration for the Chewbacca defense in South Park?
answer_text: Johnnie Cochran and his closing argument in the O.J. Simpson trial: "If it doesn't fit, you must acquit."

question_text: X, a co-founder of Magnum Photos, is considered the pioneer of street photography and candid photography. He set out to create a photographic essay capturing the essence of India after independence. This gave him exclusive access to Mahatma Gandhi on 29 January 1948, during which he took many of the portraits that are now popular. Though he has documented the likes of Camus, Picasso, and Matisse, it is his pictures of seemingly unimportant moments of ordinary life that are wildly popular, because they exhibit the "creative fraction of a second," where the photographer must know with intuition when to click the shutter. In 1952, he published a book, Images a la Sauvette, with a collection of such images. The English-language edition, though, was given a three-word title alluding to the intuitive essence of his candid/street photography. ID X and the English title.
answer_text: X = Henri Cartier-Bresson; English title = The Decisive Moment

question_text: The neuronal basis for this has been observed in fruit flies and mice, but no conclusive studies for it exist in human beings. There are, however, certain hypotheses to explain this occurrence/syndrome/phenomenon, such as: adenosine and orexin hypothesis; parasympathetic activation; insulin-induced hypokalemia. Chances are a lot of us have casually used this term for ourselves at some point, most likely on social media. What are we talking about?
answer_text: Postprandial somnolence, also known as a food coma

question_text: What connects the following in the 21st century (non-exhaustive): Mount Mabu, Mozambique; Kamil Crater, Egypt; Ancient Roman Villa, Sorbolo in Parma; Saroo Brierley.
answer_text: Google Earth: each was discovered or became famous through the use of Google Earth

question_text: A three-word phrase (fill in the blank) has its origin in a 2017 Reddit thread where users posted images which have a thematic/composition similarity that is instantly recognisable, coinciding with Wally Koval launching an Instagram account in June 2017. These include buildings and landscapes with pops of colour, symmetry, and quirky stand-out details. answer_text: Accidentally Wes Anderson, the Instagram account and book; Wes Anderson wrote the foreword

question_text: In the late 1960s, international banks were struggling with a 'paperwork crisis' amid rising trade. They relied on a slow, manual, and insecure network of teleprinters which lacked encryption and a standardized language for instructions. The Bretton Woods collapse also accelerated the creation of this neutral, member-owned cooperative, which required a more instantaneous solution as opposed to the slow teleprinters to handle currency volatility. What now modern-day backbone was created in 1973 as a result, with its HQ in Brussels?
answer_text: SWIFT, the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication

question_text: Originally designed in England in 1937 by John and Isaac Miller, this item came to be known by its now popular name only in the 1960s, thanks to actor Ryan O'Neal's character in the TV series Peyton Place. Its characteristics include a snug fit around the waist with an expandable elastic bottom hem, two buttoned flap pockets at a 45 degree angle, a tartan interior lining, and a straight collar with a button fastener. Give the keyword.
answer_text: The Harrington jacket, originally made by Baracuta

question_text: "But at that moment, I saw the true face of football, where players would give their whole lives in a stadium, with people shouting with joy and others bruised deep in their souls." What moment is referee Pierluigi Collina talking about?
answer_text: The 1999 UEFA Champions League Final, Manchester United's dramatic injury-time comeback win over Bayern Munich
